hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Thailand on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Thailand on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Thailand?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Thailand is the baht.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Bangkok?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Thailand is Bangkok.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Thailand?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Thailand article.

questions.proof: The founding of Bangkok as the capital city, was the start of the Rattanakosin Kingdom (1782–1932).

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Thailand about 513,120 square kilometres; Philippines about 343,448 square kilometres; Vietnam about 331,690 square kilometres; Sri Lanka about 65,610 square kilometres.
